modelName: One skill, one NDC — dead ends, bottleneck, reciprocity, and the third degree
modelNote: The teach chain for a single skill, drawn only from completed (badged) transactions. Four readings come off the shape without computing a single centrality score: dead ends where the skill stopped, the bottleneck every path runs through, the reciprocity asymmetry at the origin, and how many hops the skill has actually travelled against Snowden's three-degree target. Built 2026-08-31 with Marc Pierson. EVIDENCE: every arrow here is marked "asserted" because this file is an illustration. Drawn from the real badge ledger every arrow would be "observed" — a signed record rather than a self-report — which is the whole reason this method is stronger on SODOTO data than on anything else we hold. IAD LEVEL: operational (asserted 2026-08-31, open to correction at the Ostrom Workshop). Tracks a capability propagating between participants. The bottleneck reading — remove the origin and the capability leaves — is a CONSTITUTIONAL question (who has standing to teach) that this drawing raises but does not depict.

nodes.label: Skill: publish a FedWiki page. Six badged transactions. Every reading below comes from looking at the shape — nothing here is calculated.
nodes.note: Six arrows, because six badges were issued and accepted. "Read the shape" is the claim that dead ends, the bottleneck, the reciprocity asymmetry and the hop count are all visible to an untrained group in a room — no centrality score, no ranking of people, nothing that needs a tool to verify. That is the whole argument for drawing this rather than computing it.

nodes.label: MARC
nodes.note: Every path to this skill starts here. That is not a compliment — it is the single point of failure, and the coordinatorless goal is precisely the goal of making this node removable.

nodes.label: A
nodes.note: Badged nine weeks ago. Has taught nobody since. The skill arrived and stopped.

nodes.label: B
nodes.note: Badged. Has taught nobody. Dead end.

nodes.label: C
nodes.note: Badged. Has taught nobody. Dead end.

nodes.label: D
nodes.note: The only one of the four who passed it on. One hop from Marc. Whatever D did differently is the thing worth finding out — and it is a question you would never have asked without this drawing.

nodes.label: E
nodes.note: Two hops from Marc. Learned from D, taught F. The skill is now propagating without the origin touching it.

nodes.label: F
nodes.note: Three hops from Marc — the deepest the skill has travelled, and exactly Snowden's stated limit. Currently a dead end, but a new one; ask again in a month before calling it a failure.

nodes.label: DEAD END — received the skill, never passed it on. Three of the first four.
nodes.note: Allee's dead link, and the propagation question SODOTO exists to answer. A 75% dead-end rate at the first hop says the SEE-DO half is working and the TEACH half is not. That is a fixable, specific problem — quite different from 'engagement is low'.

nodes.label: BOTTLENECK — every path to this skill runs through one person. Remove him and the capability leaves with him.
nodes.note: The reading that decides whether the NDC is coordinatorless yet. It is answered by looking, not by computing betweenness — and looking is the version a group in a room can argue with.

nodes.label: RECIPROCITY — four taught out, none back. The same shape as the CHW.
nodes.note: Allee's exchange-analysis question again, on completely different data. When the same asymmetry shows up in the coop value network and in the teach chain, it is a pattern in how the work is organised rather than a fact about either individual.

nodes.label: THREE DEGREES — Snowden's limit, reached exactly once, along one path.
nodes.note: Snowden's design target is that anyone can reach help through no more than two intermediaries. One path here reaches three hops; every other path dies at one. Two numbers worth putting on a control chart: completed teach transactions per month, and how many people sit two or more hops from the origin.

edges.label: taught
edges.note: Completed — and the only one of the four that went anywhere.

edges.label: taught
edges.note: The first hop the origin had nothing to do with. This edge is the whole point of SODOTO.
